title: How funeral parades began and how Rene started a club
summary: Rene says the custom started on street corners, and describes forming the White Roses after a man was shot.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Well, did the customer having bums and funerals start with the clubs, or? Well, it seems to me like this.
Well, it seems to me like this.

It started with the club. Mostly what I think it started with, from what I can understand, from what I learnt, about 50 or 60 years back, it started from the corners. Like a good fellow was hanging on the corner, you know, and he would die. Well, they would wreck up some money and they would get a band and all his friends would march, you see. That's what I learnt, it started from, then I think it went into the clubs and dipped in places. But I think I learnt that it started from the corner. A good fellow died and said, well, now we're going to bang, you see. Because I did that many times myself. I set up clubs and I don't have that. Many times I went out begging and played for a fellow, played a few and didn't get but a dollar. Sometimes he didn't get nothing. He picked up money, you know, for a band. I paid the rest, not going to pay. And that's the way it started. As far as a lot of people can remember. Because that's been going on a long time.
Well, having some of the clubs been going on for a long time, too?

Yeah, sure. The club has been going on a long time, too. Mostly in fact, they tell me that's how clubs were formed. Because when I formed the White Rose, Lost Set Roses, White Roses, that's how we started. A fellow by the name of Bonte, he got shot. And when we marched there, and when we got in there, I said, I was about setting up the club. Who all want to set up the club, raise their hand up. It started right there. Got about nine and ten of them. Then I set up a quorum up, see. They say, you be the president. I said, well, now, who make it? Vice President. Then they took a fellow and had a bar and made it and buy a friend. See? Clumped itself too long ago. They thought I was in all that just to make some money. Which, that's always on my end, was the first thing I had them to do given little parties, you know? Little four piece band. They had the band playing. Sometimes they make money. All the money had to go to pay the band. That's what they didn't like. Plenty of them dropped out of it. I got about eight, ten dollars out of it. They got out of the seven. When they got out of the seven, you know, you split up, you know? They hadn't had no charter, nothing like that yet. It was too small. But after they had gone out of the seven, the man said, well, this is it. We don't have nothing but the staff here. We don't have no more club. It's the staff here over, because we could buy this money between hours seven. They're all right, they may have mine at night. I got mine. They're four to one club, they.
